transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I hope it's okay that I'm here. I feel a little silly coming in, honestly, because I know everyone deals with stress, but... well, my sleep has just gotten really unreliable lately. 

I go to bed completely exhausted, but then I just lie there replaying my sales forecasts and, you know, little team issues at work. And then even if I do drift off, I end up waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning, and I just can't get my brain to power down again. It's probably not a huge deal, and I really don't want to sound like I'm just complaining, but it's making my days a bit tough to get through. Is that... does that make sense as a reason to come in?
Have you noticed any changes in your mood, like feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, especially around the time your sleep problems started?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I mean, I definitely don't feel hopeless. I have a really great job and a good life, so I'd feel terrible complaining like that. I still really enjoy my weekends and seeing my friends, as long as I'm not too exhausted from being awake all night. 

It's really just... my brain won't stop buzzing about work. I hope it's okay that I don't have those other things you mentioned? I'm not really sad or down, just... a bit wound up all the time. Am I explaining that right?
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about things related to work or other responsibilities, even when you're not at work, and does it feel hard to control those thoughts?

Yeah, um, I guess I do do that. I really try not to, because I know I should just leave work at work, right? But... yeah. It's exactly like you said. 

I can literally tell myself out loud, 'Brenda, you've done the plan, just let it go.' And I really try to! But then, I don't know, maybe five minutes later I'm right back in another loop about the numbers or the team. It's like... if I manage to check one concern off my mental list and tell myself it's fine, three more just immediately pop up to replace it. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound completely neurotic? I just really want to do a good job for my team, but I admit it is a little hard to turn it off when I get home. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have you noticed any physical signs like restlessness, muscle tension, or feeling easily fatigued, especially when you're trying to relax or during the day?

Um, well... I guess I do feel a little bit of that. I mean, I hope it's normal for someone with a demanding job to feel a bit... tense? 

It's just that I feel, I don't know, wound up almost all the time. Like... like I'm sitting right in the middle of a major pipeline review, even when I'm just at home eating dinner. And my shoulders... they just stay tight. I really try to relax them, I do, but they just seem to stay hitched up by my ears no matter what I do. 

I don't want to make it sound worse than it is, though. I know everyone gets tired, and I'm probably just letting the stress get to me more than I should. Does that... I hope that answers your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms of excessive worry, difficulty controlling thoughts, and physical manifestations such as restlessness and muscle tension occurring in the context of stress related to work, without evidence of depression or significant impairment in daily functioning, align more closely with Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1). Other candidates, such as F43.22 (Adjustment Disorder with Anxiety) and G47.01 (Insomnia Disorder), are ruled out due to the chronic and pervasive nature of the anxiety, which extends beyond a situational stress response and is better captured by F41.1.

No clear exclusion yet.
